passages.title: A New Classmate
paragraphs: Leo joined our class on Monday. He was nervous（紧张的） and spoke very quietly. I asked him to sit next to me. At lunch, we talked about our hobbies. I love football, but he likes drawing. I thought we had nothing in common. Then he showed me a picture of his favourite football player. What a surprise! Now I teach him to play football, and he helps me draw. We do not have to enjoy all the same things to make friends. Sometimes our differences（不同之处） make school life more interesting.

passages.title: My Favourite Place at School
paragraphs: My favourite place at school is a small reading corner beside the library window. There is a soft chair and a shelf（架子） of storybooks. When I finish my work, I often spend a few minutes there. I like adventure（冒险） stories because they take me to places far away. Once, I read about a boy who crossed a desert （沙漠）. I almost forgot the time! The corner is quiet, but it never feels empty. Every book has something new to tell me. I always look forward to my next visit.

passages.title: Breakfast for My Family
paragraphs: Last Sunday, I decided to prepare（准备） breakfast for my family. I washed some tomatoes and put bread on three plates. Dad helped me cook the eggs because the pan（平底锅） was hot. I wanted everything to look perfect（完美的）, but I dropped a piece of bread on the floor. I threw it away and took another piece. Soon, breakfast was ready. Mum smiled when she saw the table. “This is a lovely surprise!” she said. The meal was simple, but I felt proud（自豪的）. Now I want to learn to cook something new.

passages.title: A Better Weekend Plan
paragraphs: On Friday evening, I made a long list of things to do. I wanted to finish my homework, play basketball and visit my cousin. “Can you do all these things in one morning?” Mum asked. She was right. I needed a better plan. I put the most important（重要的） jobs first and left time to take a break. I also kept Sunday afternoon free in case something changed. By Sunday evening, most of my list was finished. A good plan should be useful（有用的）, but it should also leave room for surprises.

passages.title: The Club We Chose
paragraphs: Our school opened two new clubs this term. I wanted to join the science club, but my best friend Amy chose the drama（戏剧） club. At first, I was disappointed（失望的）. I hoped we could do everything together. Then Amy said, “We can tell each other about our clubs after school.” That sounded fun. Now I carry out simple experiments （实验）, and Amy practises acting. Sometimes she asks me to watch her show. Sometimes I show her what I have made. We have different interests, but we still get on well with each other.

passages.title: A Small Change for Better Health
paragraphs: I often felt tired in the morning because I went to bed too late. I liked reading one more comic after Mum said goodnight. Last month, I decided to change this habit（习惯）. Now I pack my schoolbag before dinner and stop reading at half past eight. I also leave my tablet（平板电脑） outside the bedroom. The first few nights were difficult, but soon I began to fall asleep earlier. Now I wake up with more energy（精力）. I can pay attention in class and enjoy playing outside after school.

passages.title: The Day I Missed the Bus
paragraphs: Yesterday, I spent too long looking for my sports shoes. When I reached the bus stop, my bus was leaving. I wanted to run after it, but the road was busy. I stayed on the pavement（人行道） and called Dad. He helped me check the next bus time. Luckily, another bus came ten minutes later. I arrived at school just in time for the first lesson. That evening, I put my shoes beside my schoolbag. Getting things ready the night before is much easier than searching（寻找） for them in a hurry.

passages.title: A Different Kind of Birthday
paragraphs: For my eleventh birthday, I did not want a big party. I wanted to spend the afternoon with Grandpa. He cannot walk very far, so we had a picnic in his garden. I made a sandwich for him, and he told me stories about his childhood（童年）. Then he gave me a little wooden（木制的） boat. “I made it for you,” he said. The boat was not expensive, but I held it carefully. We took a photo together before I left. I will treasure（珍惜） that afternoon for a long time.

passages.title: Our Class Book Sale
paragraphs: Our class held a book sale to raise（筹集） money for new playground balls. We brought books from home and checked that the pages were clean. Then we divided（分配） the jobs. Some pupils made signs, while others wrote prices（价格） on small cards. I helped younger children choose books. One girl could not find a story about animals, so I searched every box with her. At last, we found one about a lost puppy. She smiled and bought it. By working together, we sold many books and made the sale a success（成功）.

passages.title: Learning to Ride Again
paragraphs: I fell off my bicycle last spring. My knee soon got better, but I was still afraid to ride. One Saturday, Dad took me to an empty playground. “We can start slowly,” he said. I put on my helmet （头盔） and held the handlebars（车把） tightly. Dad walked beside me while I tried to keep my balance（平衡）. After several short rides, I felt safer. Then I rode all the way to the gate by myself. I was not fast, but I was moving again. I was glad I did not give up.

passages.title: Shanghai Then and Now
paragraphs: Grandma showed me a photo of her old street in Shanghai. There were low houses and many bicycles. “We knew almost everyone here,” she said. Today, tall buildings stand near her home, and we can travel across the city by underground（地铁）. Shopping is easier too, because there are more shops nearby. Yet Grandma still enjoys walking to the small market. The shopkeeper（店主） knows her name and always says hello. Shanghai has changed in many ways, but friendly greetings（问候） can still make a busy street feel like home.

passages.title: A Visitor in Our Neighbourhood
paragraphs: A visitor（来访者） stopped near our school and asked for the library. I knew the way, but I spoke too quickly at first. He looked confused（困惑的）, so I tried again. “Go straight ahead and turn left at the traffic lights. The library is opposite （在……对面） the bank.” I pointed to the buildings as I spoke. Then I told him about the park behind the library. He thanked me and set off. Giving directions（方向指引） is not just about knowing a place. It is also about helping another person understand clearly.

passages.title: A Journey by Underground
paragraphs: On Saturday, Mum let me plan our underground（地铁） journey to a museum. I studied the map and found two possible routes（路线）. One was shorter, but we had to change trains twice. The other took a little longer and needed only one change. We chose the second route（路线） because it was easier. At the station, I checked the signs before we got on the train. We reached the museum before it opened. I felt like a real guide （向导）. Next time, I want to plan our journey home as well.

passages.title: Behind a Bowl of Rice
paragraphs: At lunch, I used to leave rice in my bowl when I felt full. Then our class visited a farm. A farmer showed us the young rice plants and explained（解释） how he cared for them. The plants need water, sunlight and time to grow. When the rice is ready, farmers must harvest（收割） it. More work follows before it reaches our kitchen. I looked at my lunch differently that day. Now I help myself to a smaller amount（数量） first. If I am still hungry, I can always ask for more.

passages.title: A Festival by the River
paragraphs: Last year, my family watched dragon boat races during the Dragon Boat Festival. People stood along the river and cheered （欢呼） as the boats passed. A drum（鼓） beat loudly, and the rowers（划船的人） moved together. My little brother wanted to know why the boats were so long. Dad explained（解释） that each boat needed room for a team. After the races, we shared some zongzi at home. Grandma made both sweet and salty ones. I liked the sweet ones best. The festival brought our family together and gave us plenty to talk about.

passages.title: The Library on Wheels
paragraphs: Every other Wednesday, a colourful van stops in a village square. It is a library on wheels. Inside, there are shelves of books for children and adults（成年人）. The nearest large library is far away, so this van makes borrowing（借用） books much easier. A librarian（图书管理员） helps readers find what they need. They can return their books when the van comes again. One boy always arrives early to choose a new animal story. For him, the van brings more than books. It brings something exciting to look forward to.

passages.title: One Seed, Two Pots
paragraphs: Our teacher gave us two bean seeds and asked us to find out how light affects（影响） their growth. We planted them in matching pots with the same soil（土壤）. One pot stood by the window, while the other stayed in a dark cupboard（柜子）. We gave both pots the same amount（数量） of water. After several days, both seeds began to grow. The plant in the cupboard became pale（苍白的） and weak. The one by the window grew green leaves. We wrote down our observations （观察记录）. A fair comparison （比较） helped us understand what we saw.

passages.title: Where Does Rainwater Go?
paragraphs: After a heavy shower, small streams（小股水流） of water run along our street. Some water enters drains（排水又） and travels through pipes（管道）. In the park, some soaks（渗入） into the ground. Plants can take in water through their roots （根）. Water in puddles（水洼） may slowly disappear when it changes into water vapour（水蒸气） and rises into the air. This process is called evaporation（蒸发）. Clouds can form when water vapour cools and becomes tiny drops. Later, water may fall as rain again. A rainy afternoon is part of a much bigger journey that happens over and over again.

passages.title: A Tree through the Seasons
paragraphs: There is a tree outside my bedroom window. In spring, tiny green leaves appear on its branches（树枝）. Birds sometimes stop there and sing. In summer, the leaves grow thick and give us shade（阴凉处）. I like reading under the tree when the weather is warm. Autumn brings yellow leaves that fall onto the path. By winter, most branches are bare（光秃秃的）. The tree looks quiet, but it is still alive. I take a photo of it every month. Looking at the pictures side by side helps me notice changes I might otherwise（否则） miss.

passages.title: Busy Bees in the Garden
paragraphs: On sunny days, bees visit the flowers in our school garden. They collect（收集） a sweet liquid（液体） called nectar（花蜜）. As they move inside a flower, some pollen（花粉） sticks to their bodies. When they visit another flower, they may carry it there. This helps many plants make seeds. Bees are small, but their work matters to gardens and farms. Our class planted more flowers near the fence to provide（提供） food for them. We watch quietly and keep our distance. There is no need to touch a bee to learn something interesting about it.

passages.title: An Old T-Shirt’s New Life
paragraphs: My favourite T-shirt became too small, but I did not want to throw it away. Mum suggested（建议） making a bag from it. First, we laid it flat on the table. With Mum’s help, I cut off the sleeves（袖子） and made the neck opening wider. Then we cut strips（条带） along the bottom and tied them together tightly. Soon, the old T-shirt became a shopping bag. I tested it with two light books before using it outside. It was not perfect （完美的）, but it was reusable（可重复使用的）. An old thing can turn into something useful.

passages.title: A Picnic with Less Rubbish
paragraphs: Before our class picnic, we discussed how to make less rubbish. I packed my lunch in a reusable（可重复使用的） box instead of a plastic bag. My friend brought a water bottle and a cloth napkin（餐巾）. At the park, we shared fruit and ate most of our food. We put the leftovers（剩余食物） back into our boxes to take home. Before leaving, we checked the grass carefully and picked up every piece of rubbish. Our picnic was still fun, but there was less to throw away. A little preparation （准备） made a clear difference.

passages.title: The Missing Lunch Box
paragraphs: At lunchtime, my blue lunch box was missing. I checked my bag twice, but it was not there. Then I noticed（注意到） a similar（相似的） box on Sam’s desk. “Is that mine?” I asked. Sam opened it and laughed. It held noodles, but mine held rice. Our teacher asked about my morning. I remembered showing my new bag to Lucy near the window. There was my lunch box, behind a plant! I thanked everyone for helping me look for it. A simple clue（线索） solved the mystery（谜团）.

passages.title: The Wallet beside the Gate
paragraphs: On my way home, I found a brown wallet（钱包） beside the school gate. There was money inside, but no telephone number. For a moment, I wondered what I should do. Then I took it to the school office. A teacher asked me where I found it and wrote down the details（详细信息）. Soon, a worried visitor（来访者） returned to ask about a lost wallet. The teacher checked his name before giving it back. His face filled with relief（宽慰）. I felt happy too. I helped turn a bad afternoon into a better one.

passages.title: The Kite in the Tree
paragraphs: A sudden gust（一阵强风） of wind blew our kite into a tree. Ben wanted to climb up, but the branches（树枝） looked thin. “Let’s think of another way,” I said. We asked a park worker for help. He checked the tree and brought a long pole（长杆）. We stood back while he carefully lifted the string from a branch. Soon, the kite floated down. One corner was torn（撕破的）, but we could repair（修补） it at home. We thanked the worker and moved to an open field. There was more space to fly our kite safely there.

passages.title: The Fox and the Empty Basket
paragraphs: A fox found a basket of apples beside a wall. He could carry it alone, but two small rabbits offered to help. “No,” he said. “Then I would have to share.” He pulled the basket towards his home. It was heavy, so he stopped to rest. When he lifted it again, the old bottom broke. Apples rolled down the hill and into a stream（小溪）. The fox ran after them, but they floated away. He returned to the empty basket. “Next time, I will accept help and share,” he thought. A few apples would be enough（足够的） for him.

passages.title: Two Friends and a Broken Model
paragraphs: I left my model bridge on the classroom table. When I returned, one side was broken. Jack was standing nearby, so I blamed （责怪） him immediately（立刻）. His face turned red. “I didn’t touch it,” he said. Then our teacher explained（解释） that wind through the open window blew a book onto it. I felt ashamed（惭愧的）. I said sorry to Jack for blaming him without asking questions. He accepted（接受） my apology （道歉） and offered to help. We repaired the bridge together. Next time, I will find out what happened before deciding who is responsible（负有责任的）.

passages.title: When the Lights Went Out
paragraphs: We were watching television when the lights suddenly went out. My little sister held my hand because the room was dark. Dad found a torch（手电筒）, and Mum checked that everyone was safe. We sat together near the window while we waited. At first, I missed the television. Then Grandpa began telling a funny story about his schooldays. Soon, we were all laughing. When the electricity（电） came back, nobody reached for the remote control（遥控器）. “Finish the story first!” my sister said. Our quiet evening turned out to be more interesting than we expected （预料）.

passages.title: The Race I Did Not Win
paragraphs: I trained for the school race for three weeks. On sports day, I started well and ran near the front. Then the boy beside me fell. I stopped and helped him move off the track（跑道）. A teacher came over, and I joined the race again. I finished far behind the winner and felt disappointed（失望的）. Later, the boy came to thank me. I still wanted to win, but helping him was more important（重要的）. Winning matters to me, yet it is not the only thing I can be proud of.

passages.title: A Letter to My Future Self
paragraphs: Dear Future Me, next year you will be at secondary school（中学）. Are you still interested（感兴趣的） in science? Have you made any new friends? Right now, I feel excited and a little worried about the change. I hope you remember how you learned to speak in front of our class. You practised, made mistakes and tried again. When something seems difficult, please be patient with yourself. Keep asking questions, and make time for the people you care about. I cannot know everything about your life, but I hope you are still curious（好奇的）. Love, Your Younger Self
